edits.headline: Spain's Pedro Sánchez calls a snap election after housing protests
edits.subheadline: The general election will be held on 29 November, The National reported.
editorialBody: Spain's prime minister, Pedro Sánchez, has called a snap general election after protests over housing, The National reported. The vote will be held on 29 November. CNBC also reported on the decision.
Flávio Bolsonaro has taken a commanding lead in Brazil's election, the Financial Times reported.
Executives from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and Meta are set to testify at a New York City Council hearing on the risks of artificial intelligence, CNBC reported.
CNBC reported a suspected case of plague in Russia that has reportedly been linked to the death of a laboratory worker.

A Russian envoy said increased strikes on Ukraine were aimed at preventing attacks on the Russian economy, TASS reported. Russia's military said its troops had taken the Samoilovka community in the Zaporozhye region, according to TASS. A Russian MP said Ukraine faced armed revolt because of corruption and failures at the front, TASS said.
A Flydubai co-pilot allegedly planned to crash an Israel-bound jet at Ben Gurion Airport, Fox News reported.
An investigation into a fatal paragliding crash in Hong Kong found that the 74-year-old pilot lost control in strong winds, the South China Morning Post reported.

Michael Saylor's company, Strategy, bought 334 bitcoin for $28.7 million, taking its holdings above 848,000 BTC, The Block reported. The dollar neared its strongest level this year, Bloomberg reported.
Zach Bryan broke Ed Sheeran's stadium record after defying Kraft over Palestine, The Canary reported.
